a.xlink:title: C · Known despair already permits ordinary loss. A river verse confined to that case would add nothing.
C · The river permission therefore reaches lack of awareness, even with a mark and even where learning would not produce despair.

a.xlink:title: C · The special permission could concern owners pursuing the object and expressly refusing despair; ordinary loss without despair could still be prohibited.
R · Permit all irrecoverable losses and ordinary unmarked loss before awareness, as Rava; prohibit ordinary marked loss before actual despair. Exception permission can coexist with Rava’s position.
R · Ordinary unmarked loss before awareness is prohibited. The tested shortcut does not establish this conclusion by itself.
C · Read the verse as addressing the very instant of loss, whether the owner knows or not.
a.text: C · Read the verse as addressing
whether the owner knows or not.

a.xlink:title: C · At that instant, complete permission is stated only for loss to everyone; ordinary recoverable loss remains prohibited, including unmarked loss.
C · Under Rashba’s temporal reading, ordinary unmarked loss is prohibited before awareness. This records his interpretation, not a machine proof.
